domains.name: Monitoring, Logging, Analysis, Remediation, and Performance Optimization

tasks.name: Implement highly available and resilient environments.

concepts.name: EC2 Auto Scaling
concepts.description: Automatically adjusts EC2 capacity in an Auto Scaling group to match demand and maintain desired capacity.

concepts.name: Auto Scaling capacity bounds
concepts.description: Minimum, desired, and maximum capacity constrain how many capacity units an Auto Scaling group should maintain.

concepts.name: Target tracking scaling
concepts.description: Adjusts Auto Scaling group capacity to keep a selected utilization or throughput metric near a target value.

concepts.name: Step scaling
concepts.description: Adjusts capacity by different amounts depending on how far a CloudWatch alarm metric breaches configured thresholds.

concepts.name: Scheduled scaling
concepts.description: Changes Auto Scaling group capacity at known times based on a schedule.

concepts.name: Predictive scaling
concepts.description: Uses historical workload patterns to forecast future capacity needs and proactively adjust capacity.

concepts.name: Instance warmup
concepts.description: Excludes newly launched instances from some aggregated scaling decisions until their initialization period is complete.

concepts.name: Health check grace period
concepts.description: Temporarily delays Auto Scaling health-check replacement decisions for newly launched instances while they initialize.

concepts.name: Launch templates for Auto Scaling
concepts.description: Reusable EC2 launch configuration such as AMI, instance type, security groups, and other instance settings.

concepts.name: CloudFront caching
concepts.description: Caches content at edge locations so requests can be served without repeatedly contacting the origin.

concepts.name: CloudFront cache key
concepts.description: Determines whether viewer requests map to the same cached object based on selected request values.

concepts.name: CloudFront cache policy
concepts.description: Controls cache-key composition and cache TTL behavior for a CloudFront cache behavior.

concepts.name: CloudFront origin request policy
concepts.description: Controls which viewer request values are forwarded to the origin without necessarily adding them to the cache key.

concepts.name: ElastiCache scaling
concepts.description: Adjusts cache capacity by changing node size, node count, shards, or replicas according to the engine and deployment mode.

concepts.name: ElastiCache for Valkey or Redis OSS
concepts.description: ElastiCache engines that support replication and, depending on mode, shards and automatic failover.

concepts.name: ElastiCache for Memcached
concepts.description: A distributed cache engine that scales horizontally by adding or removing cache nodes but does not provide Redis-style replication.

concepts.name: RDS storage autoscaling
concepts.description: Automatically increases RDS allocated storage when free space becomes low, up to a configured maximum threshold.

concepts.name: RDS read replicas
concepts.description: Asynchronous replicas that can serve read traffic to scale read-heavy workloads.

concepts.name: Aurora Auto Scaling
concepts.description: Uses Application Auto Scaling to adjust the number of Aurora Replicas based on target-tracking metrics.

concepts.name: DynamoDB capacity modes
concepts.description: On-demand capacity adapts to request traffic while provisioned mode allocates configured read and write throughput.

concepts.name: DynamoDB auto scaling
concepts.description: Uses Application Auto Scaling target tracking to adjust provisioned read or write capacity for tables and global secondary indexes.

concepts.name: Elastic Load Balancing
concepts.description: Distributes traffic across healthy targets and Availability Zones according to the selected load balancer type.

concepts.name: Application Load Balancer
concepts.description: Layer 7 load balancer for HTTP and HTTPS with content-based routing capabilities.

concepts.name: Network Load Balancer
concepts.description: Layer 4 load balancer for high-performance TCP, UDP, and TLS traffic.

concepts.name: Gateway Load Balancer
concepts.description: Distributes traffic to fleets of virtual network appliances using the GENEVE protocol.

concepts.name: ELB target groups
concepts.description: Groups registered targets and defines routing and health-check configuration for load balancers.

concepts.name: ELB health checks
concepts.description: Probe registered targets and route traffic only to targets that meet health criteria.

concepts.name: Cross-zone load balancing
concepts.description: Allows a load balancer node to distribute traffic across healthy targets in all enabled Availability Zones.

concepts.name: Deregistration delay
concepts.description: Allows in-flight requests to complete while a target is draining after deregistration begins.

concepts.name: Route 53 health checks
concepts.description: Monitor endpoint or calculated health and can influence DNS responses.

concepts.name: Route 53 failover routing
concepts.description: Uses primary and secondary DNS records so Route 53 can answer with a secondary endpoint when the primary is unhealthy.

concepts.name: Route 53 Evaluate Target Health
concepts.description: For supported alias records, uses the health of the AWS resource or referenced records when choosing DNS answers.

concepts.name: RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment
concepts.description: Maintains a synchronous standby in another Availability Zone for high availability and automatic failover; the standby does not serve reads.

concepts.name: RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster
concepts.description: A three-AZ RDS deployment with a writer and two readable standby instances for high availability.

concepts.name: ElastiCache Multi-AZ
concepts.description: Promotes a replica automatically when a Valkey or Redis OSS primary becomes unavailable, reducing write downtime.

concepts.name: EFS availability classes
concepts.description: Regional EFS stores data across multiple Availability Zones, while One Zone stores data within a single Availability Zone.

concepts.name: FSx high availability
concepts.description: Selected Amazon FSx file systems offer Multi-AZ or high-availability deployment options with failover.

concepts.name: Highly available web tier
concepts.description: Combines multiple Availability Zones, load balancing, and scalable compute to reduce the impact of instance or AZ failures.

concepts.name: AWS Backup
concepts.description: Centralized service for policy-based backup and recovery across supported AWS resources.

concepts.name: AWS Backup plans
concepts.description: Define backup schedules, windows, lifecycle, retention, and optional copy rules for assigned resources.

concepts.name: AWS Backup vaults
concepts.description: Containers for recovery points with access-control and encryption settings.

concepts.name: AWS Backup copies
concepts.description: Copies recovery points to another vault, Region, or account when supported.

concepts.name: AWS Backup restore testing
concepts.description: Automates periodic restore jobs to validate that selected recovery points can be restored and to measure restore duration.

concepts.name: EBS snapshots
concepts.description: Point-in-time backups of EBS volumes that can be used to create new volumes.

concepts.name: Amazon Machine Images
concepts.description: Templates for launching EC2 instances that can include block device mappings backed by EBS snapshots.

concepts.name: RDS backups and snapshots
concepts.description: Automated backups support retention and point-in-time recovery, while manual snapshots persist until deleted.

concepts.name: RDS point-in-time recovery
concepts.description: Restores an RDS database to a selected time within its restorable backup window by creating a new DB instance.

concepts.name: DynamoDB on-demand backups
concepts.description: User-initiated full table backups that remain available until deleted.

concepts.name: DynamoDB point-in-time recovery
concepts.description: Continuous backups that can restore a DynamoDB table to a selected second within the configured recovery period, up to 35 days.

concepts.name: S3 Versioning
concepts.description: Retains multiple object versions and uses delete markers to protect against many accidental overwrites and deletions.

concepts.name: S3 replication
concepts.description: Asynchronously copies eligible objects between buckets in the same or different Regions; RTC adds a predictable replication-time SLA.

concepts.name: FSx for Windows shadow copies
concepts.description: Point-in-time file-system snapshots that let users restore prior file or folder versions quickly.

concepts.name: Amazon FSx backups
concepts.description: File-system backups used for retention and recovery; they are separate from user-facing shadow copies.

concepts.name: RTO and RPO
concepts.description: RTO limits acceptable service restoration delay; RPO limits acceptable data loss measured from the last recoverable point.

concepts.name: Backup and restore DR
concepts.description: Lowest-cost DR strategy that provisions infrastructure and restores data after a disaster.

concepts.name: Pilot light DR
concepts.description: Keeps core data and essential infrastructure available in the recovery Region while most application capacity is not running until failover.

concepts.name: Warm standby DR
concepts.description: Keeps a scaled-down but fully functional environment running in the recovery Region and scales it up during failover.

concepts.name: Multi-site active/active DR
concepts.description: Runs the workload in multiple Regions serving traffic simultaneously for very low recovery times at greater cost and complexity.

concepts.name: RDS instance class scaling
concepts.description: Changes the compute and memory resources of an RDS DB instance by modifying its DB instance class.

concepts.name: AWS DataSync scheduled replication
concepts.description: Schedules data transfer between supported storage systems, including replication between file systems for protection and migration.

concepts.name: Queue-driven scaling
concepts.description: Queue-driven scaling adjusts worker capacity based on outstanding work, often using backlog per worker rather than CPU alone.

concepts.name: Amazon SQS
concepts.description: Managed message queue service for decoupling and buffering asynchronous work.

concepts.name: SQS Standard queues
concepts.description: At-least-once, best-effort ordered high-throughput queue type.

concepts.name: SQS FIFO queues
concepts.description: Queue type for ordered processing and duplicate-suppression semantics.

concepts.name: SQS dead-letter queues
concepts.description: Queue used to isolate messages that repeatedly fail processing.

concepts.name: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)
concepts.description: DynamoDB-compatible in-memory cache for microsecond eventually consistent reads.

concepts.name: Aurora Serverless v2
concepts.description: Aurora configuration that automatically scales DB compute capacity in ACUs.

concepts.name: Amazon Application Recovery Controller
concepts.description: Service for application recovery capabilities such as zonal shift for supported resources.

concepts.name: AWS Storage Gateway
concepts.description: Hybrid storage service providing file, volume, and tape-style interfaces backed by AWS storage.

concepts.name: EC2 Auto Scaling Instance Refresh
concepts.description: Rolling replacement mechanism for updating an Auto Scaling group fleet.

concepts.name: Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks
concepts.description: Hooks that pause launch or termination transitions for custom actions.

concepts.name: Auto Scaling warm pools
concepts.description: Pool of pre-initialized instances for faster scale-out.

concepts.name: Amazon ECS
concepts.description: Managed container orchestration service.

concepts.name: AWS DataSync
concepts.description: Managed data transfer service for supported storage locations.

questions.prompt: New Auto Scaling instances need about four minutes to start. The load balancer marks them unhealthy after one minute, so Auto Scaling replaces them too early.

steps.prompt: Which setting is the most direct reason healthy-starting instances are being replaced too early?

choices.label: The health check grace period is shorter than real startup time
The instance warmup is longer than the health check grace period
A simple-scaling cooldown is too long
The Auto Scaling maximum capacity is too high

steps.prompt: After confirming the application normally needs four minutes to become healthy, what is the best next action?

choices.label: Set startup/health timing to reflect real readiness, then verify the health check

questions.explanation: Health check grace period protects a new instance from health-based replacement while the application starts. Instance warmup serves a different purpose: it keeps fresh capacity from distorting scaling decisions too early. Because replacement happens before the app is healthy, fix the grace period first.
hints: Separate 'when can health checks replace this new instance?' from 'when should its metrics influence scaling?'

questions.prompt: A CloudFront distribution serves the same product images to every viewer, but its cache hit ratio is poor. Flag the cache-key inputs that create unnecessary cached variants.

elements.label: Accept-Language is in the cache key because the origin actually returns localized image metadata
A unique X-Request-ID header is in the cache key even though it does not change the response
The `size` query string is in the cache key because it changes which image size the origin returns
A per-user tracking cookie is in the cache key even though all viewers receive identical content

questions.explanation: A cache-key value should vary the cache only when it can change the origin response. A unique request ID and an irrelevant tracking cookie create needless variants and lower the hit ratio. Keep language or size in the key only when they change the returned representation.
hints: Ask one question for each input: can changing this value change the response body that should be cached?

questions.prompt: Order what happens when an ALB target repeatedly fails its configured health check and later recovers.
